The 24-Month STEM OPT Extension is an additional benefit from United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) that allows international students in F-1 status who receive a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in an approved STEM field to apply for a 24-month extension of their standard 12-month Post-OPT period, twice in a lifetime. This allows international students the opportunity to gain additional off-campus work experience in their field of study after completion of course studies and Post-OPT.
F-1 status international students who receive a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in an approved STEM field.
F-1 students must currently be participating in the 12-month Post-OPT, and working for a U.S. employer in a job directly related to their major area of study.

F-1 students must have earned a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree from a school that is accredited by a U.S. Department of Education-recognized accrediting agency and that is certified by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) at the time of application.
F-1 students must have successfully completed a bachelor's, master’s, or doctoral degree in a STEM field included in the DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List.
F-1 students may not engage in practical training for less than 20 hours per week during the STEM OPT extension period.
F-1 students may not engage in practical training that is unpaid/volunteer work or self-employment.
F-1 students may not be in a multiple employer arrangement or employed by a sole proprietorship, through a temp agency, or through a consulting firm arrangement that provides labor for hire.
F-1 students must work with their employer to complete an individualized Training Plan for STEM OPT Students (Form I-983).
Students participating in STEM OPT are responsible for ensuring that all employment information reported to the ISSC, SEVP, and/or U.S. government agencies is complete, accurate, and truthful.
Reporting false employment, submitting fraudulent documentation, or misrepresenting job duties may result in serious immigration consequences.
F-1 students participating in a 12-month period of Post-OPT based on a non-STEM degree may be eligible to use a previous STEM degree for a STEM OPT extension.
If students earn another qualifying STEM degree at a higher educational level, they may be eligible for one additional 24-month STEM OPT extension.
Employer must be registered with the E-Verify Employment Verification System and remain a participant in good standing with E-Verify, as determined by USCIS.
Employer must have a valid Employer Identification Number (EIN) issued by the Internal Revenue Service for tax purposes.
Employer must provide a practical training opportunity that is commensurate with those of similarly situated U.S. workers in duties, hours, and compensation.
Employer must implement a formal training program to augment the F-1 student’s academic learning through practical experience.
Employer must maintain a bona fide employer-employee relationship with the F-1 student.
The employer that signs the Form I-983 must be the same entity that provides the practical training experience to the student.

The employer may not be the F-1 student’s employer in name only and may not assign, or otherwise delegate its training responsibilities to a non-employer third party (for example, a client or customer of the employer).
Employer must report any material changes of the F-1 student’s employment by filling out a modified Form I-983.
If applicable, the employer must report the F-1 student’s termination of employment or departure to the Designated School Official (DSO) within 5 business days.
F-1 students seeking STEM OPT extensions may be employed by new start-up businesses so long as all regulatory requirements listed above are met.
Apply for 24-Month STEM OPT no more than 97 days prior to end date of your Post-OPT.

facts.value: There are no employer or location restrictions for authorized STEM OPT, but the job must be in the U.S.
You must carry your I-20, passport, and valid F-1 visa stamp to re-enter the U.S.
Entering the U.S. on any visa other than F-1 will invalidate your F-1 status and STEM OPT.
The primary purpose of Post-OPT/STEM is working; taking classes can be incidental.
Pursuing a new degree program will invalidate your Post-OPT/STEM once you receive the new degree I-20.
There is a 60-day grace period after Post-OPT/STEM ends to change visa status, transfer, or return home.
Changing your address while your STEM OPT application is pending may cause issues with your EAD card.
You must update your address through MyUSCIS, USPS, and MyASU within 10 days of moving.
Your SEVP Portal account will lock after 3 consecutive incorrect password entries or 45 days of inactivity.
To reset your password, follow the steps to reset using your ASU Public Email and SEVIS ID.
You can check the status of your application by logging into your USCIS online application.
The ISSC takes up to 7 days to process Post-OPT/STEM requests; USCIS average processing time is 90 days.
